title: When a Moth Lands on You
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: A moth landed on my hand. Dot had rules.
first_visual: A woman's open hand on a dark kitchen table; a moth with eye-marked wings settles on her knuckles.

beats.visual: A moth settles on Ivy's knuckles; its wings show eyes.
beats.vo: A moth landed on my hand. Dot had rules.

beats.visual: Ivy's other hand rises to swat, then stops; she holds her breath.
beats.vo: One: don't swat. Two: don't breathe on it.

beats.visual: The window reflection shows the kitchen behind her: empty.
beats.vo: Three: don't move until it leaves.

beats.visual: Macro: the wing-eyes are angled past her shoulder.
beats.vo: Its wings weren't looking at me. They were looking behind me.

beats.visual: The moth lifts off toward the lamp.
beats.vo: 'It only leaves when it's done. Or scared.'

beats.visual: Key moment: Ivy turns; the Tenant inches away, lamp-eyed, smiling.

ending: It flies to the lamp. Ivy turns: the Tenant, inches away, lamp-eyed, smiling.

originality_review: Original. It avoids moths at a porch light and 'don't open the door', and uses our own Watcher moth (brand emblem concept B). The hook avoids the 'If ___ ever... DO THIS' template. Moth folklore is used generically, not from any creator.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Dot's rules for a moth landing on you: don't swat, don't breathe, don't move until it leaves. Ivy obeys and notices the wing-eyes are staring past her. The moth was holding something behind her at bay, and when it flies, that thing is free.

hooks.line: A moth landed on my hand. Dot had rules.
hooks.first_visual: A woman's open hand on a dark kitchen table; a moth with eye-marked wings settles on her knuckles.

hooks.line: Don't swat it. Don't breathe on it. Don't move.
hooks.first_visual: A hand trembling, the moth perfectly still.
An old woman in a teal cardigan, smiling.

hooks.line: Its wing-eyes weren't looking at me.
hooks.first_visual: Wing eye-markings aimed over a shoulder.

hooks.line: It only leaves when it's done. Or when it's scared.
hooks.first_visual: A moth lifting off a hand.

setting: Ivy's kitchen at night; one lamp; the dark window.
conflict: Ivy's urge to swat against Dot's folk rules.
escalation: Breath held; the reflection shows nothing; the wing-eyes aim past her shoulder.
reveal: The moth was a guard watching the thing behind her.
emotional_objective: Brand anchor: the Watcher moth as protector.
